report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/lanes/checks.py chunk 1 of 2: documented WriteAttempt, CheckPolicy, AST helpers, and four baseline checks; all docstring claims verified against this chunk.
risks: daedalus/lanes/checks.py:47-65 | medium | WriteAttempt.creating defaults to False; a caller constructing WriteAttempt(rel, proposed, repo_root) without original may unintentionally treat a created file as an edit, triggering edit-only checks. | Check all WriteAttempt constructions in the codebase for explicit creating argument.

daedalus/lanes/checks.py:106-115 | low | toplevel_defs returns None on RecursionError, treating deeply nested code as unparsable; parses then attempts ast.parse again, which may also raise RecursionError and be caught. | Confirm that ast.parse RecursionError is caught in parses (it is, line 115) and that the fallback path is acceptable.

daedalus/lanes/checks.py:177-178 | low | _exports sets opaque=True when __getattr__ is defined, but does not check that __getattr__ is module-level and callable; a class method named __getattr__ would not trigger. | Verify the intended semantics: should any top-level __getattr__ definition mark opaque?

daedalus/lanes/checks.py:171-178 | low | _exports marks opaque=True on star-imports, but does not consider dynamic imports (e.g., __import__) or other dynamic name provision. | Confirm whether such patterns are expected in this repo.

daedalus/lanes/checks.py:196-207 | medium | parses has a fallback branch that returns '' when toplevel_defs(attempt.proposed) is None and not creating and original is unparsable. This means a proposed file that fails to parse but was already unparsable before is allowed, which may contradict the docstring's promise that unparsable proposed content is refused. | Check if the intended behavior is to allow replacement of unparsable files with unparsable content.

daedalus/lanes/checks.py:231-236 | low | not_truncated uses len() on strings, which counts Unicode code points, not bytes; a file with multibyte characters could have a different byte size ratio. | Confirm whether byte-size comparison is intended.

daedalus/lanes/checks.py:240-249 | low | no_elision uses substring matching on lowercased text; a marker that is a substring of a larger word (e.g., '...' appears in 'foo...bar') could trigger false positives. | Confirm whether exact word-boundary matching is needed.

handoff.purpose: Defines WriteAttempt, CheckPolicy, shared AST helpers, and the first four baseline checks (parses, not_truncated, no_elision, not_substituted).

symbols.name: BASELINE_POLICY
symbols.note: Default CheckPolicy instance with default values.

symbols.name: CheckPolicy
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding per-lane policy dials: elision_markers, min_size_ratio, min_symbol_survival, min_symbols_to_judge, first_party_roots, max_named_imports.

symbols.name: WriteAttempt
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass describing a file write attempt: rel, proposed, repo_root, original, creating. Provides is_python property.

symbols.name: parses
symbols.note: Baseline check: refuses Python files that do not parse. Runs on created files too.

symbols.name: not_truncated
symbols.note: Baseline check: refuses proposed content shorter than min_size_ratio of original.

symbols.name: no_elision
symbols.note: Baseline check: refuses output containing a new elision marker.

symbols.name: not_substituted
symbols.note: Baseline check: refuses Python edits whose proposed top-level definitions share none with the original.

symbols.name: toplevel_defs
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of top-level function/class names, or None if source does not parse.

symbols.name: _module_path
symbols.note: Resolves a dotted module name to a file, __init__.py, or namespace directory; returns None if not found.

symbols.name: _exports
symbols.note: Returns (top-level names, opaque) from a Python file; opaque indicates star-import or __getattr__.

claims.text: Cheapest first, first refusal wins, fail-closed.
claims.why: The chunk defines checks but does not show the ordering or fail-closed enforcement; that is in run_checks (not in this chunk).

claims.text: A check returns "" to pass and a human-readable reason to refuse; a check that RAISES is treated as a refusal
claims.why: The chunk does not contain run_checks, which would implement the raise-to-refuse behavior.

claims.text: the first four arguments are bundled into WriteAttempt
claims.why: WriteAttempt fields rel, proposed, repo_root, original correspond to the four arguments.

claims.text: Two of the baseline checks need a fifth fact (is this file being CREATED, so that there is no original to compare against)
claims.why: WriteAttempt has a creating field; parses and not_substituted both check attempt.creating (lines 198 and 226).

claims.text: The dataclass grows instead.
claims.why: WriteAttempt is a dataclass with fields; adding a field is the growth mechanism.

claims.text: ``original`` is the exact current text, or "" when ``creating``.
claims.why: Field default is "" and creating defaults to False; the docstring describes the intended usage.

claims.text: Keeping the two facts separate rather than inferring "creating" from an empty original matters: a lane that truncates a real file to nothing must not be able to present that as a creation and skip the guards that only run on edits.
claims.why: The dataclass separates original and creating; checks use attempt.creating and attempt.original independently (e.g., not_truncated checks both).

claims.text: Only refused when the marker is NEW, so a file that legitimately contains the phrase does not become unwritable.
claims.why: no_elision checks marker in proposed and not in original (lines 241-244).

claims.text: Below this fraction of the original size, a "full rewrite" is a truncation.
claims.why: not_truncated compares len(proposed) >= min_size_ratio * len(original) (line 232).

claims.text: Below this fraction of surviving top-level definitions, a "rewrite" is a different file rather than an edited one.
claims.why: The threshold is used in not_substituted, but the survival calculation is in the next chunk (the function is cut off).

claims.text: 0.5 is deliberately permissive: a genuine refactor can rename or merge a lot, and refusing a real change costs twice -- the work is lost AND the task escalates to a paid lane. The failures this exists to catch were TOTAL substitutions (0% survival), so a loose threshold still stops them.
claims.why: The comment is a rationale; the default value 0.5 is set. The behavior is implemented in the next chunk (not visible here).

claims.text: Below this many top-level definitions the survival ratio is noise -- losing one of two functions is an ordinary edit.
claims.why: The field exists with default 3; usage is in not_substituted (next chunk).

claims.text: A missing first-party module is a file the model invented.
claims.why: The field exists with default roots; the imports_resolve function (not in this chunk) implements the check.

claims.text: Only the TOP level: a rewrite is free to reorganise nested helpers, and counting those would make ordinary refactors look like substitutions.
claims.why: toplevel_defs iterates tree.body only, which is the top level.

claims.text: A directory WITHOUT __init__.py still counts. Since Python 3.3 such a directory is an implicit namespace package (PEP 420) and imports perfectly well -- tools and tests in this repository are exactly that, and both import fine while reporting __file__ is None.
claims.why: _module_path checks namespace.is_dir() and any(namespace.glob("*.py")) (lines 159-160).

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30: without this branch the gate reported "module 'tools' does not exist" for tests/test_iron_plan_guard.py, a real committed file that imports it, and test_no_false_positives_across_the_real_tree failed with its own message -- "this gate must never refuse real repo code". Any lane writing a module that imports tools or tests would have been refused for importing something that is demonstrably there.
claims.why: The measurement and test are external; the chunk only shows the code that fixes the issue.

claims.text: This does not loosen the guard. The invented imports it exists to catch -- daedalus.linting, daedalus.wiki_vault -- name directories that do not exist either, so they are still refused.
claims.why: The claim depends on the actual repository contents, not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: A directory is required to contain at least one .py file, so an empty or data-only folder cannot launder an import that would fail at runtime.
claims.why: The namespace branch requires any(namespace.glob("*.py")) (line 160).

claims.text: The returned directory is deliberately not a readable module: _exports fails closed on it (an OSError becomes opaque=True), which is the honest answer, because what a namespace package provides is its submodules and no single file lists them.
claims.why: _exports catches OSError and returns (frozenset(), True) (lines 177-178).

claims.text: opaque means static reading is not authoritative for this module -- it star-imports or defines a module-level __getattr__, either of which can legitimately provide a name no reader can see.
claims.why: _exports sets opaque=True when a star import is found (line 170) or when a top-level __getattr__ is defined (line 166).

claims.text: A Python file that will not parse is not an improvement.
claims.why: parses returns a refusal message when ast.parse fails (lines 211-219).

claims.text: Runs on CREATED files too, which is where the hole was: an edit that stops parsing was caught by not_substituted as a side effect, but a brand-new module that does not parse had nothing looking at it -- the imports check returns early on a parse failure, calling it "a different guard's business". This is that guard.
claims.why: parses does not return early on creating; it checks attempt.is_python and then parses the proposed content regardless of creating (lines 196-219).

claims.text: The classic full-rewrite failure: the model returned part of the file.
claims.why: not_truncated compares lengths and refuses when proposed is below the ratio.

claims.text: The model admitting, in prose, that it dropped code.
claims.why: no_elision looks for elision_markers in proposed text.

claims.text: Only NEW markers count. A file that already contained the phrase would otherwise become permanently unwritable by this lane.
claims.why: no_elision checks marker in proposed and not in original (lines 241-244).

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30, and the reason this exists. A change request naming two files is sent once per file; asked to rewrite daedalus/shift.py the model returned the contents of tests/test_shift.py. The module was destroyed and the run reported status: done. Three of five multi-file writes failed exactly this way.
claims.why: The measurement is external; the chunk cannot verify the historical incident.

claims.text: None of the other guards can see it. Truncation compares SIZE, and a substituted file is a perfectly normal size -- the test module was in fact larger than the module it replaced. Elision looks for a model admitting it omitted something, and nothing was omitted: a complete, valid, well-formed file arrived. It was simply the wrong one.
claims.why: not_truncated only compares sizes; no_elision only looks for markers; not_substituted compares top-level names, which is a different signal.

claims.text: So this asks the only question that separates the two cases: does the result still contain the thing that was sent? An edit keeps most of a file's top-level names; a substitution keeps none of them.
claims.why: not_substituted computes before and after toplevel_defs and (in the next chunk) checks survival.

claims.text: Deliberately Python-only. The check needs a parser to be meaningful, and a guess about other languages would either fire on ordinary edits or provide false assurance for files it cannot actually read.
claims.why: not_substituted returns '' for non-Python files (line 226: if not attempt.is_python).

observations.what: WriteAttempt.creating defaults to False, so a caller constructing WriteAttempt without specifying creating for a new file will be treated as an edit, causing edit-only checks to run.
toplevel_defs returns None on RecursionError, treating deeply nested code as unparsable; parses then attempts ast.parse again, which may also raise RecursionError and be caught.
_exports sets opaque=True when __getattr__ is defined, but does not check that __getattr__ is module-level and callable; a class method named __getattr__ would not trigger.
_exports marks opaque=True on star-imports, but does not consider dynamic imports (e.g., __import__) or other dynamic name provision.

parses has a fallback branch that returns '' when toplevel_defs(attempt.proposed) is None and not creating and original is unparsable. This means a proposed file that fails to parse but was already unparsable before is allowed, which may contradict the docstring's promise that unparsable proposed content is refused.
not_truncated uses len() on strings, which counts Unicode code points, not bytes; a file with multibyte characters could have a different byte size ratio.
no_elision uses substring matching on lowercased text; a marker that is a substring of a larger word (e.g., '...' appears in 'foo...bar') could trigger false positives.
